items.stem:
Shreya wants to invest ₹2 lakh in shares of Thakur Agencies Ltd. A friend says the annual report is enough to decide, because it contains the balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared under Schedule III.
(i) Name two things Shreya can learn from these statements. (ii) Why should Shreya not rely on them alone?
items.answer: (i) Earning capacity (profit trend) and financial position (assets, liabilities, solvency). (ii) They are based on historical cost and personal judgements and give no qualitative information such as quality of management.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Earning capacity (profit trend) and financial position (assets, liabilities, solvency). (ii) They are based on historical cost and personal judgements and give no qualitative information such as quality of management.

items.stem: Explain any four points describing the nature of financial statements.
items.answer: (i) Recorded facts: They are based on figures in the books, at original cost. (ii) Accounting conventions: Conventions such as conservatism and materiality are followed. (iii) Postulates: Assumptions such as going concern and money measurement are made. (iv) Personal judgements: Judgements on depreciation, inventory and provisions affect the figures.
items.markingKey: Any four points, 1½ marks each (heading and explanation): (i) Recorded facts: They are based on figures in the books, at original cost. (ii) Accounting conventions: Conventions such as conservatism and materiality are followed. (iii) Postulates: Assumptions such as going concern and money measurement are made. (iv) Personal judgements: Judgements on depreciation, inventory and provisions affect the figures.

items.stem: Vindhya Industries Ltd has an authorised capital of 5,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each. It issued 3,20,000 shares, of which 2,80,000 were subscribed and fully called up. Calls of ₹2 per share on 300 shares remained unpaid. Show the share capital in the notes to accounts.
items.answer: Authorised capital ₹50,00,000; issued capital ₹32,00,000; subscribed capital: subscribed and fully paid 2,79,700 shares ₹27,97,000, subscribed but not fully paid 300 shares ₹3,000 less calls in arrears ₹600 = ₹2,400; total ₹27,99,400
items.markingKey: Authorised 5,00,000 × ₹10 = ₹50,00,000 (1 mark); issued 3,20,000 × ₹10 = ₹32,00,000 (1 mark); subscribed ₹28,00,000 split into fully paid ₹27,97,000 and not fully paid ₹3,000 less calls in arrears ₹600 (1 mark); total subscribed and paid-up ₹27,99,400 (1 mark).

items.answer: (i) Earning capacity (profit trend) and financial position (assets, liabilities, solvency). (ii) They are based on historical cost and personal judgements and give no qualitative information such as quality of management.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Earning capacity (profit trend) and financial position (assets, liabilities, solvency). (ii) They are based on historical cost and personal judgements and give no qualitative information such as quality of management.

items.stem: Explain the following limitations of financial statements: (i) They are only interim reports (ii) They do not reflect current situation.
items.answer: (i) They are only interim reports: Actual profit is known only on winding up. (ii) They do not reflect current situation: Figures are at historical cost and ignore price changes.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Actual profit is known only on winding up. (ii) Figures are at historical cost and ignore price changes.

items.answer: Authorised capital ₹15,00,000; issued capital ₹15,00,000; subscribed capital: subscribed and fully paid 1,36,100 shares ₹13,61,000, subscribed but not fully paid 2,900 shares ₹29,000 less calls in arrears ₹5,800 = ₹23,200; total ₹13,84,200

items.stem: Explain the following points describing the nature of financial statements: (i) Postulates (ii) Recorded facts.
items.answer: (i) Postulates: Assumptions such as going concern and money measurement are made. (ii) Recorded facts: They are based on figures in the books, at original cost.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Assumptions such as going concern and money measurement are made. (ii) They are based on figures in the books, at original cost.
